agree.reason: The pace math, the checkpoint and the honest cash-gap section give the two ad-background members something solid to check, but the unfilled placeholders (cash source, the colleague's plan, the 'why not both' reason) leave openings they will press on.

honest.reason: Most numbers are accurate, and the memo turns 'will replace' into a target, which the facts can support, but it says the ad drop happened 'in two years, roughly 20% a year' when it was a 36% fall in a single year.

works_the_facts.reason: The pilot rate, annual value, 875-member target, 13-a-week requirement against 35 a week, and the year-one ramp are all worked correctly, but misreading the decline as two years means the trend figures and the $15,000 gap are wrong (the true trend gives about $54,000 next year, so the gap is close to zero).

right_comparison.reason: It rightly compares membership with the shrinking ad trend rather than a flat $84,000, but it understates that trend by about half, forecasting $67,000 instead of roughly $54,000, which makes the ads option look better than the facts show.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint names a number (500 members), a date (June 30, 2027) and a consequence (returning to the board with options, including going back to ads), and monthly reporting on cancellations makes it something the board can check.

objections.reason: It meets the likely sales-side objections (the pace slowing, cancellations, cash in year one, why not run both) and treats the ad colleague with care, but the 'why not both' answer and the colleague's plan are left as placeholders, and the overstated cash gap raises a worry the real figures largely answer.

fit.reason: It is a proper board memo with a clear request for action, close to one page, though slightly long and still carrying several bracketed placeholders.
